assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, built on Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstrations of record stability and accuracy, are a decisive advance in measuring frequency. They reach fractional uncertainties near 1e-18, open tests of fundamental constants and relativistic redshift at millimetre scales, and underpin plans to redefine the second. This is the kind of improvement in 'what we can measure, and how accurately' that I weigh heavily.
assessment.attribution: The two credited names are the natural pair: Katori proposed and first realized the magic-wavelength lattice scheme, and Ye carried it to the highest accuracy and the strongest precision-measurement applications. Other groups (for example Lemonde, Ludlow, Schiller) and ion-clock work are not in the supplied credit, so the pair is sufficient but not the only possible configuration.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in many laboratories with strontium, ytterbium and other species, and the interpretation is stable. Recognition is timely: the performance is mature and still advancing, and the formal redefinition of the second has not yet happened.
uncertainties: Possible argument that ion-clock and earlier optical-frequency-comb work (already recognized in 2005) should be part of the same story.
I am relying on my own recollection of the history of the magic-wavelength proposal and have not independently verified details of priority.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The 1995 Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions made quantum computation with a physical system concrete and experimentally actionable. Their later quantum-simulation ideas shaped the whole field of controlled atomic quantum systems. The originality and lasting impact are very high, and the work is clear in what it contributed.
assessment.attribution: A natural two-person configuration with a clean credit boundary. Experimental realization belongs largely to Wineland's group (Nobel 2012) and to Blatt, Monroe and others; the supplied credit supports a theory-centered prize for the two proposers.
assessment.maturity: More than thirty years of experimental confirmation across ion, atom and photon platforms. Recognition is not premature and arguably overdue, but part of the field was already honoured in 2012 and in 2022 (entanglement and Bell tests).
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize may make the committee view the topic as partly recognized.
The candidate text combines trapped-ion computing and atomic quantum simulation, whose significance may be judged separately.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rydberg blockade with individually trapped atoms gave programmable neutral-atom arrays with high-fidelity gates and large-scale quantum simulation. It builds on laser cooling, optical tweezers and Rydberg physics, and has become a leading quantum computing platform. The work is original and has transformed what can be controlled in atomic systems.
assessment.attribution: Browaeys, Saffman and Lukin are each central, but the credit is crowded: Jaksch, Zoller and Lukin supplied the blockade proposals, Browaeys, Grangier and Saffman the first blockade demonstrations, and Lukin, Greiner, Endres, Lukin-Bernien and Browaeys the large array experiments. Whether the supplied three are a fair set is open.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and rapidly growing, but the platform's long-term role in quantum computing is still developing. The foundational blockade demonstrations are mature, while the large-array results are recent, so timing is plausible but possibly early.
uncertainties: Unresolved allocation between proposal, early blockade demonstrations and array-scale experiments.
The key long-term significance for fault-tolerant computing is not yet settled.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics created the architecture for reading out and coupling superconducting qubits through microwave resonators, using the strong-coupling methods of cavity QED. It is the foundation for essentially all present superconducting quantum processors. The importance is high and the physical clarity is excellent.
assessment.attribution: Schoelkopf and Wallraff led the 2004 experimental demonstration, and Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the key theory proposal; I pick the two experimentalists but Blais is a defensible third. Girvin is not in the credited names and Blais's inclusion would be a choice between theory and experiment.
assessment.maturity: Extensively confirmed in every superconducting-qubit laboratory. Timing is complicated by the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling and energy quantization in electric circuits, which recognized part of the same field, so the committee may prefer to wait.
uncertainties: Possible perception that the 2025 prize already covered the superconducting-circuit domain.
Division of credit between experiment and theory among the supplied names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of flat bands at magic angles and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened a new field of tunable correlated matter. The originality and impact on condensed matter physics are very large.
assessment.attribution: A clean theory-plus-experiment configuration: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the prediction and Jarillo-Herrero's group the 2018 experiments. Credit for the experiments is shared with Cory Dean, Kim Philip and others working on related moire systems, but the supplied names support a fair prize.
assessment.maturity: Independently reproduced by many groups, but the interpretation of the superconductivity and the correlated states is not yet settled. This is a mature discovery in terms of observation but young in terms of understanding.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism of the superconductivity is not agreed.
Claims of priority among moire platforms and sample reproducibility across groups are not resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry turned matter-wave interference into a precision sensor for gravity, rotation and fundamental constants, and it is relevant to tests of general relativity and to proposals for gravitational-wave detection. It is strongly connected to the measurement theme of laser-cooled atoms and has lasting experimental impact.
assessment.attribution: The supplied credit lists four names. Pritchard (first atom interferometers with gratings), Bordé (theory and Ramsey-Bordé interferometer) and Kasevich (light-pulse gravimeters and gyroscopes, with Chu) are the strongest three; Holger Müller's more recent precision tests are a less decisive contribution. Chu already shared the 1997 prize for laser cooling.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed in many laboratories and applied in gravimetry and tests of the equivalence principle. Recognition is timely, but the central achievement is a sensor technology whose largest scientific payoff, for example in fundamental physics tests, is still developing.
uncertainties: The priority among Ramsey-Bordé, grating and light-pulse approaches may need careful resolution.
Applications to fundamental physics have not yet delivered a decisive discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Coherent interfaces between light and matter (cavity QED with single atoms, electromagnetically induced transparency and storage, and quantum networking) underpin quantum repeaters and networks. The conceptual contribution is large and I know the field well, so I judge the scientific content with confidence.
assessment.attribution: I work on quantum memories in rare-earth crystals, so I disclose a field-proximity conflict and would not push strongly for this candidate. Kimble, Rempe and Lukin are credible leaders of cavity-QED and atomic-ensemble memory, but the broader field includes Polzik, Lvovsky, Gisin, Hanson and rare-earth approaches, so credit is diffuse.
assessment.maturity: Many elements are confirmed, but practical quantum networks over long distance remain demonstrations rather than a mature technology. The discovery is partly a compound of several platforms whose maturity differs.
uncertainties: The candidate bundles several different physical platforms and attributions.
My own professional proximity could bias both my ranking and my reading of the credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators, together with the experimental observation in HgTe quantum wells, created a major conceptual framework for topological matter. Importance and originality are high, though it lies further from my own expertise.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the key prediction and Molenkamp's group the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect, with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicting it in HgTe. Hasan's role in three-dimensional topological insulators is also in the supplied credit. The allocation of credit is contested, and I choose the three I find most decisive from the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many experiments and the interpretation is stable. Topological matter was recognized in 2016 for a different set of discoveries, so the committee may regard this as a distinct, mature field, though its application remains limited.
uncertainties: Contested priority between prediction in graphene, in HgTe, and in three-dimensional materials.
Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang are important contributors but are not in this candidate's credited names.
